input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS 140-3 crypto remediation for KServe component images

## Description

This epic makes every KServe component image in the model serving stack run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the request path. It covers the audit, remediation, and verification of the KServe control-plane images, the FIPS regression gate for those images, and the evidence inputs (module inventory, build attestations, test results) for the KServe portion of the compliance evidence package.

## Scope

- Audit all KServe component images for cryptographic library usage, producing a per-image module inventory that classifies each linked crypto library as validated or non-validated and identifies request-path usage.
- Remediate every KServe image so that the request path uses only validated cryptographic modules on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters (rebuilds, library replacements, or base-image changes as the audit dictates — the remediation mechanism per image is an implementation decision for the team).
- Verify correct serving behavior (inference request path) for the remediated images on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Author and verify the FIPS regression gating CI check covering the KServe images: a gating check that fails any KServe build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. This epic owns the portion of the stack-wide FIPS regression enforcement (HLR-3) that covers the KServe surface.
- Produce build attestations for every remediated KServe image and hand off the per-image module inventory, attestations, and FIPS test results as inputs to the compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists for every KServe component image, classifying each linked cryptographic library as validated or non-validated and recording request-path usage.
- Every remediated KServe image runs correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster with no non-validated crypto in the inference request path, demonstrated by test results captured per image.
- The FIPS regression gating check fails a KServe build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage and passes a clean build (verified with a deliberate negative test), and it is wired as a gating check in the KServe build pipeline.
- Build attestations are produced for every remediated KServe image and are available to the compliance evidence package.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — KServe portion: all KServe component images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules.
- **HLR-3 (P1, bundled)** — this epic authors and verifies the FIPS regression gating check covering the KServe images it remediates; the check spans exactly the same images and build pipeline as the remediation, so it is not separately schedulable from this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P0, partial input)** — produces the KServe module inventory, build attestations, and test results consumed by the compliance evidence package.

# Compliance evidence package assembly and certification submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results covering every serving-stack image — and submits it through the security review board to the external accredited certification laboratory. It runs after the serving-stack image remediation work (KServe control plane, serving-runtime data plane, and Platform Operator) has produced its per-surface inventories, attestations, and test results.

## Scope

- Define the evidence package structure: the module inventory, build attestations, and FIPS test results required per serving-stack image, in the format the security review board and certification lab accept.
- Aggregate and reconcile the per-surface module inventories, build attestations, and test results produced by the image remediation work into a single, internally consistent package covering every serving-stack image.
- Run the package through the mandatory security review board sign-off at the defined milestones, incorporating required corrections.
- Submit the approved package to the external accredited certification laboratory and drive the submission through triage.

## Risks / Notes

- The accredited laboratory's turnaround is historically six to nine months, and the security review board meets on a fixed cadence; both are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. Certification completion is therefore a schedule risk on this epic, not an acceptance criterion — the acceptance criteria below sit on the deliverable and submission, which the engineering work controls.
- Workbenches, pipelines, and training FIPS posture, and Common Criteria certification, are out of scope for this strategy and excluded from the package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains a module inventory, build attestations, and FIPS test results for every serving-stack image (KServe control plane, serving-runtime data plane, Platform Operator), with no gaps or unresolved contradictions between per-surface inputs.
- The evidence package passes the security review board sign-off required at the defined milestones.
- The evidence package is submitted to the external accredited certification laboratory and the submission is accepted for triage.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — this epic assembles the compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) and submits it through the security review board to the external certification lab.

# FIPS support posture and cluster-prerequisite documentation

## Description

This epic documents the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, as an outcome of the FIPS 140-3 compliance work. It is a docs-authoring epic through the Red Hat docs content process and runs after all implementation work in the strategy has landed.

## Scope

Content outline (authored inside the documentation set for the model serving stack):

- FIPS support posture: what is supported (validated crypto modules in the serving-stack request path), what is certified vs. compliance-ready, and the current certification status of the evidence package submission.
- Cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation: what operators and administrators must configure on the OpenShift cluster to run the serving stack in FIPS mode.
- Scope boundaries as documented posture: workbenches, pipelines, and training FIPS posture are covered by separate strategies; Common Criteria is out of scope.
- Operational guidance covering the FIPS regression gating checks now enforced in the serving-stack build pipelines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack, including the certification status of the compliance submission.
- Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for running the serving stack on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented FIPS remediation and the submitted evidence package (reviewed by the engineering teams that did the work), and review sign-off is recorded.
- The documentation follows the Red Hat docs content process for authoring, building, and publishing.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. Epic priority is P0 via the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy frontmatter priority: Critical).
